one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled catalyst falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30. Qualcomm has reported fiscal Q4 on a Wednesday 38 days after fiscal year-end three years running (FY23 Nov 1, FY24 Nov 6, FY25 Nov 5), and FY26 ended Sep 27, which points to Wed Nov 4, 2026, after the window (supervisor finding; no scheduling 8-K yet). Things that do fall in the window: peer and supply-chain reads (TSMC and memory-maker earnings in mid/late October, smartphone sell-through), macro prints, and any unscheduled Amazon/data-center news. Pre-earnings positioning into Nov 4 could add some late-October volatility. Consensus revisions have been flat for 30 days (FY27 $10.20, Dec-qtr $2.30), so there is no fresh estimate-momentum signal. The September run-up to ~$206 and the -7% reversal on Sep 28 leave momentum and reversal roughly cancelling. So I center on $184.5 with no drift and a monthly sigma of about 14.5% (a bit under 54%/3.5 = 15.4%, because the 54% realized vol is inflated by the April-June spike), with a lognormal spread. This is essentially unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%: FY28 non-GAAP EPS est. $11.30 x 16.5x = $186) and FCF yield (40%: normalized FY28 pre-SBC FCF ~$11.0B / ~1,060M shares = ~$10.40/share at a 5.5% yield = $189). That gives about $187 as the value the market should put on the stock by Sep 2027, when it will price off FY28 earnings. The EPS base is re-based to the $10.20 non-GAAP FY27 consensus and the FCF normalization is corrected.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Sep-2028 FY) non-GAAP EPS $11.30 x 16.5x forward non-GAAP P/E

inputs_detail.value: $10.20 (34 analysts, range $8.83-12.24); FY26 $10.48; Dec-qtr $2.30 vs $3.50 a year ago; FY27 was $10.96 90 days ago and $10.20 for the last 30 days
Data center ~$5B; non-handset growth >60% y/y, replacing roughly all FY26 Apple product revenue; QCT Android revenue -20% y/y (>$1.50 EPS headwind); handset market down low teens

~1,080M diluted at FY27 start (1,069M Q3 diluted + 17.8M Modular shares issued Jul 28, after quarter-end); buybacks ~$1.4B/qtr retire ~7-8M shares/qtr; Amazon warrant ~0.5M net shares on the treasury method

inputs_detail.derivation: Start from the FY27 consensus of $10.20 (company non-GAAP basis). Add: data-center revenue ramping from ~$5B toward $8B at below-QCT gross margin with opex growing slower than revenue (+$0.55); partial recovery of the >$1.50 Android EPS headwind as memory costs normalize (+$0.40); double-digit price increases lifting QCT gross margin back toward 48-50% net of the 1.5-2pt custom-silicon drag (+$0.25); net share count down ~2%/yr from buybacks (+$0.20). Subtract the residual Apple modem roll-off beyond FY27 (-$0.30). Total about $11.30, about +11% y/y. That is well below the straight-line path to the >$18 FY29 target, which I haircut because data-center execution is unproven.

On a consistent non-GAAP basis the stock trades at ~18.1x FY27 ($184.5/$10.20). Handset-era QCOM traded around 12-17x non-GAAP. I pick 16.5x: a premium to the handset-era middle for the data-center/auto mix shift, but below today's 18x because FY27 estimates fell ~7% in 90 days, SBC (~$3.4B/yr) is a large share of non-GAAP EPS, and the Street is mostly Hold (22 of 37). In round 1 I used 17x against a wrong 19.8x-on-$9.30 base; on the right base I trim it by half a turn.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Normalized FY28 pre-SBC FCF ~$11.0B / ~1,060M diluted shares = ~$10.40/share, capitalized at a 5.5% FCF yield

inputs_detail.value: $8,405M / $1,578M; includes a -$1,798M inventory build; the -$5,550M 'income tax payments in excess of provision' line offsets the non-cash $5.7B valuation-allowance release (deferred tax assets rose from $743M to $5,679M); SBC $2,579M

inputs_detail.derivation: Add back the one-off $1.8B inventory build to 9M OCF, giving ~$10.2B, or ~$13.6B annualized. That is a little high as a steady state because of working-capital timing, so I take ~$12.8B of normalized OCF at the FY27 EPS level. Grow it ~+5% with FY28 EPS net of the lower-margin data-center mix, to ~$13.3B. Subtract higher capex of ~$2.3B/yr (9M capex was $1.6B vs $0.8B a year ago on the data-center build). Result: ~$11.0B. Round 1 reached a similar level through a wrong tax add-back; the level holds on the corrected route.
Start at ~1,080M (Q3 diluted 1,069M + 17.8M Modular), less ~7-8M/qtr buybacks against $20.6B of authorization, plus <1M net from the Amazon warrant on the treasury method.

Management bought back stock at an average $222 in Q3, which implies it sees a mid-single-digit FCF yield as attractive. SBC of ~$3.4B/yr (~$3.2/share) is a real cost that is only partly offset by buybacks, which argues for a yield no lower than 5.5% on pre-SBC FCF. After SBC, that is ~3.8%, a full price for a company whose earnings are shrinking in FY27.

bear.story: The memory-driven handset slump runs through FY27, Android revenue falls more than 20%, the Apple product exit is complete by the Sep-2027 iPhone, and price increases fail to restore QCT gross margin. The ASIC ramp stays low-margin and falls short of $5B, and the HBC accelerator slips with no merchant wins. FY28 non-GAAP EPS is about $9.0 (below the FY27 consensus low end) at about 13.5x, i.e. the April 2026 low near $122.

base.story: FY27 lands near the $10.2 consensus with data center at ~$5B, auto above a $7B run rate, and handsets bottoming with a modest recovery. Gross margin returns to the 48-50% range by late FY27. FY28 EPS comes in around $11.3 at 16.5-17x.

bull.story: The Amazon collaboration scales (more warrant tranches vest as purchases build), HBC silicon wins a third data-center customer, and the path to $15B data center / >$18 FY29 EPS becomes credible. FY28 EPS is about $12.7 at a ~22.5x AI-infrastructure multiple, back toward the May 2026 peak ($260).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $125 (-32%, just above the $121.99 52-week low), the stock would be pricing ~12x the $10.20 FY27 non-GAAP consensus, the bottom of the handset-era range, with no credit for data center. That most likely means something fundamental broke: the December-quarter ASIC revenue or the ~$5B FY27 data-center target slips, gross margins stay below range despite price increases, or FY27 EPS falls toward the $8.8 low estimate. At 45-54% vol, ordinary one-sigma annual noise reaches ~$130-140, so the break level sits below that.

TSMC and memory-maker earnings: read-through on wafer/memory cost inflation and smartphone build cuts
Q1 FY27 earnings: size of ASIC revenue from the two hyperscalers, gross-margin trend after price increases
Arm v. Qualcomm Third Circuit appeal ruling (Arm appealed the Sep 30, 2025 judgment for Qualcomm)
Renewed Apple global patent license takes effect (terms undisclosed); QTL run-rate visibility
Launch of first HBC-based AI accelerator; customer silicon evaluations; possible new merchant data-center wins
Q2 and Q3 FY27 earnings: data-center ramp toward $5B and Amazon warrant tranche vesting disclosures
Amazon warrant vesting (tied to purchases up to $60B) as a public tracker of the AWS ramp; US-China export rules

key_uncertainties: Whether data-center revenue actually reaches ~$5B in FY27 from two ASIC customers, and at what gross margin (management guided a 1.5-2pt QCT GM drag from custom silicon). The $60B is the warrant-vesting ceiling, not a purchase commitment.
How long memory-cost inflation depresses Android handset volumes (market down low teens, QCT Android revenue -20%, >$1.50 EPS headwind)
Speed of the Apple modem exit (share materially below 20% on the new iPhone, ~50% sequential drop into the December quarter)
Whether double-digit price increases restore the 48-50% baseline gross margin without losing share

SBC (~$3.4B/yr) against buybacks (~$1.4B/qtr). Modular's 17.8M shares are already issued, and the Amazon warrant is only ~0.5M net shares now (<=3M if fully vested), with its cost showing up as contra-revenue as tranches vest.
Very high stock volatility (54% realized, range $122-$260 in 12 months) driven by swings in the AI narrative rather than earnings
Whether FY27 estimates keep falling: the consensus went from $10.96 to $10.20 in 90 days and has been flat for the last 30 days
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor fact-checked three errors in my round 1, and I verified each against primary data. (1) The consensus base: Yahoo's analysis page shows FY27 non-GAAP consensus of $10.20 (34 analysts), FY26 $10.48, Dec-qtr $2.30, flat for 30 days but down from $10.96 90 days ago. The $9.30 I used was TIKR's undefined 'normalized' NTM figure. So the stock is ~18.1x, not ~20x. (2) FCF: the Q3 cash-flow statement confirms the -$5,550M tax line coincides with deferred tax assets jumping from $743M to $5,679M (the non-cash valuation-allowance release), so it is not a cash one-off. The real one-off is the -$1,798M inventory build. I now normalize via inventory, and I note SBC of $2,579M for 9M in the yield choice. (3) Share base: Modular's 17.8M shares were issued after Q3, so FY27 starts near 1,080M. Rebuilt valuation: FY28 EPS $11.30 (from the $10.20 base plus the DC ramp, Android recovery, pricing and buybacks, less the residual Apple roll-off) x 16.5x non-GAAP = $186; FCF ~$10.40/share at 5.5% = $189; blend $187 (was $190). The corrections largely cancel: a higher EPS base, but a re-based lower multiple and a slightly lower FCF path. That agrees in direction with the supervisor's $185, but I reached it independently and keep a slightly higher FCF view because 9M OCF ex-inventory annualizes to ~$13.6B. Distribution: median ~$188, lognormal sigma ~0.44 (below the 54% realized, which is inflated by the April-June spike), with a slightly fatter left tail for the handset-slump plus data-center-slip bear ($120). Scenario mean is ~$196 (0.25x120 + 0.5x190 + 0.25x285). Thesis break lowered to $125 (12x corrected FY27 consensus), in line with the supervisor's point that $130 is within one-sigma noise; I agree. One-month view unchanged: the Q4 print is most likely Nov 4, outside the window. Round-2 research: 2 fetches (SEC Q3 release, Yahoo analysis page).
